Slice: Add Tool

Intent

Put a tool into the shed so neighbors can borrow it. The shed manager records the tool's name, an optional description, and its default checkout period. That period is the longest period a checkout of the tool can start with. A tool can be borrowed as soon as it is added: the Tool Catalog lists it as available (INV-TCAT-1), and Check Out Tool lends it.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Tool Inventory screen, when a new physical item joins the shed. Each physical item is added on its own, including an item identical to one already in the shed.

Command / Input

Command: Add Tool

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
toolId ToolId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new tool, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different tool already added (INV-ADD-10).
name Text yes Leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed. Must not then be empty (INV-ADD-4). Need not be unique (INV-ADD-8).
description Text no Optional. Leading and trailing whitespace removed. Empty after that means none.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int yes Whole days, 1 to 30 inclusive (INV-ADD-3). A fractional value is refused, never rounded.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Inventory @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Added → context Tools Read by: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (their own slices, right after this one); and, for the tool's name only, My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send and Flagged Neighbors.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
toolId ToolId yes From the command. Identifies the tool everywhere from here on.
name Text yes From the command, trimmed.
description Text yes Optional: absent when the command had none, or only whitespace. Otherwise from the command, trimmed.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int yes From the command: whole days, 1 to 30.
addedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

Every field is fixed for good. No command changes a tool's name, description or default period; to correct a mistake, the shed manager retires the tool and adds it again.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Added starts the new tool's entry in two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • Tool Inventory (slices/tool-inventory.md) lists the new tool for the shed manager.
  • Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) lists it to neighbors as available to borrow.

Both are eventually consistent: the new tool appears once each view has caught up with Tool Added.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-ADD-1: Only the shed manager can add a tool.
    • Neighbors do not add tools. How the shed manager is recognised is an open question below.
  • INV-ADD-2: Every tool is added with a default checkout period.
    • A checkout of this tool may start with a shorter period, never a longer one. An extension can later take a loan past it.
  • INV-ADD-3: A tool's default checkout period is a whole number of days, from 1 to 30.
  • INV-ADD-4: Every tool has a name. A description is optional.
    • A name that is empty, or only whitespace, is no name. A description that is empty, or only whitespace, is recorded as none.
  • INV-ADD-5: Each physical item is added as its own tool.
    • Two identical drills are two tools, each added separately. There is no quantity on a tool.
  • INV-ADD-8: Tool names need not be unique.
    • Two identical drills may both be named "Cordless drill". Each tool is told apart by its tool ID, not its name.
  • INV-ADD-9: Each tool gets its own tool ID when it is added, and keeps it for good.
    • The tool ID is how every later event, view and command refers to the tool. Names are only for people to read.
  • INV-ADD-10: Adding a tool with a tool ID that is already used adds nothing new.
    • A repeat with the same details, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the tool since. A repeat with different details is refused (tool-id-in-use).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds tool T1 named "Cordless drill", described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days, from the Tool Inventory screen
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded for T1 with that name, description and 7-day default checkout period, and the time it was added.
  • Tool added without a description (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Ladder" with a default checkout period of 3 days and no description
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with that name, no description, and the 3-day period.
  • Blank description is no description (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Ladder" with a 3-day period and a description of only whitespace
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with no description.
  • Whitespace around the name is removed (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named " Ladder " with a 3-day period
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the name "Ladder".
  • A second identical item (INV-ADD-5, INV-ADD-8, INV-ADD-9)
    • Given: the shed holds tool T1 named "Cordless drill"
    • When: the shed manager adds a second, identical drill as tool T2, also named "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded for T2, a separate tool with its own tool ID. The shed now has two tools named "Cordless drill", T1 and T2.
  • Shortest allowed period (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Stud finder" with a default checkout period of 1 day
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the 1-day period.
  • Longest allowed period (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Tile saw" with a default checkout period of 30 days
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the 30-day period.
  • Period over the maximum (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool named "Tile saw" with a default checkout period of 31 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • Period of zero (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool with a default checkout period of 0 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • Period that isn't a whole number of days (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool with a default checkout period of 2.5 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • No default period (INV-ADD-2)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool named "Ladder" with no default checkout period
    • Then: refused with period-missing: "A tool needs a default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • No name (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool whose name is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with name-missing: "A tool needs a name." No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager tries to add a tool (INV-ADD-1)
    • Given: the request does not come from the shed manager
    • When: it asks to add a tool
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can add tools." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days
    • When: the same Add Tool request for T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. The shed still has one tool T1.
  • The same request after the tool was retired (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days, and T1 has since been retired
    • When: the same Add Tool request for T1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. T1 stays retired.
  • A repeat that differs only in whitespace (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Ladder", 3 days
    • When: an Add Tool request arrives for T1 named " Ladder ", 3 days
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A tool ID reused for different details (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days
    • When: an Add Tool request arrives for T1 named "Ladder", 3 days
    • Then: refused with tool-id-in-use: "That tool ID is already used by another tool." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Tool Inventory screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

Reason Sentence Rule
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can add tools. INV-ADD-1
name-missing A tool needs a name. INV-ADD-4
period-missing A tool needs a default checkout period. INV-ADD-2
period-out-of-range The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30. INV-ADD-3
tool-id-in-use That tool ID is already used by another tool. INV-ADD-10

tool-id-in-use can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

A missing or malformed tool ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same tool ID and the same details, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, even if the tool has since been retired or lost. So a retry after a lost response never adds a second tool. Because identical items are legitimately added as separate tools (INV-ADD-5), a repeat is recognised by its tool ID only, never by matching names or details.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may add a tool (INV-ADD-1). How the shed manager is recognised is the identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: none. Tool Added holds only tool details, and doesn't record who added the tool.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on: none. Add Tool is the first slice on the timeline. Refusing a reused tool ID needs only the earlier Tool Added events.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (a new entry); My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send and Flagged Neighbors (the tool's name). Check Out Tool and Place Hold act on the tool by its tool ID, and Check Out Tool takes the tool's default checkout period from it.

Open Questions

  • How does the system know that the person adding a tool is the shed manager?
    • No event or slice records who the shed manager is or how they sign in. Every shed-manager action (add, retire and mark tools lost; suspend and reinstate) depends on the answer.
    • (a) The shed manager has a sign-in set up outside the model, with a shed-manager role. Nothing about it is recorded as an event. (b) The shed manager is a neighbor account given a shed-manager role, which needs an event and slice to grant it.
    • Recommendation: (a). There is one shed manager, and nothing on record asks to change who it is.
  • Are there length limits on a tool's name and description?
    • Recommendation: name up to 100 characters, description up to 500. A longer one is refused with the limit in the reason, never cut short.
"},{"index":1,"name":"Register Neighbor","x0":269.75,"x1":413.75,"docHtml":"

Slice: Register Neighbor

Intent

Let a neighbor join the tool shed by signing themselves up, so they can borrow tools. Signing up records the neighbor's name and the email address the shed uses to reach them. A new neighbor is active and can borrow straight away.

Trigger & Actor

A person who wants to join, from the Sign Up screen. They sign themselves up; the shed manager doesn't enroll neighbors. Someone whose earlier account is closed may sign up again here, as a new account. How a person is recognised once signed up is the open identity question below.

Command / Input

Command: Register Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID. Text fields have leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed; text that is empty after that counts as absent.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new account, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different account already registered (INV-REG-7).
name Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3). Need not be unique (INV-REG-9).
email Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3). Must not be held by another account under INV-REG-4. Format and comparison rules are open questions below.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Sign Up @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Registered → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors and My Account (their own slices, right after this one); and, for the neighbor's name and email, Tool Inventory (name only), Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command. Identifies the account everywhere from here on.
name Text yes From the command, trimmed.
email Text yes From the command, trimmed. The account's email until a later Neighbor Email Changed replaces it.
registeredAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the sign-up date.

The event records a fact that never changes. A later email change is its own event; the name is never changed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Registered starts the new account's entry in two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • Neighbors (slices/neighbors.md) lists the new neighbor to the shed manager as active.
  • My Account (slices/my-account.md) shows the new neighbor their account.

Both are eventually consistent: the new account appears once each view has caught up with Neighbor Registered.

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor signs themselves up; the shed manager does not enroll neighbors. Every account starts active: Neighbor Registered is the only event that starts an account, and suspension and closure come later, from other slices. The Neighbors view shows a new account as active (INV-NBRS-2), and Check Out Tool lends to it under its usual rules.

  • INV-REG-3: Sign-up requires a name and an email address.
    • The shed emails neighbors, and only by email: overdue notices to borrowers and pickup notices to holders both go to this address.
    • A name or email that is empty, or only whitespace, is missing.
  • INV-REG-4: A sign-up is refused if its email belongs to an account that is not closed, or to a closed account that was suspended when it was closed.
    • An account's email is its current one: the email it registered with, or the latest Neighbor Email Changed for it. An email an account has changed away from belongs to no one.
    • One account per email. A closed account's email can be used again, so a neighbor who left can come back with the same address.
    • An account closed while suspended keeps its email for good, so a suspended neighbor can't get around the suspension by closing their account and signing up again with the same email. A suspended neighbor can't change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email), so that email is the one they were suspended under.
    • A sign-up with a different email is accepted, even from someone whose earlier account was closed while suspended. Email is the only thing that identifies a neighbor. The shed manager sees both accounts on the Neighbors screen and can suspend the new one.
    • The same rule applies when a neighbor changes their email (INV-CEM-2, Change Email).
  • INV-REG-5: Signing up has no approval or verification step.
    • Neighbor Registered is recorded straight from the request. Nothing waits for the shed manager, and the email address isn't confirmed first. The new neighbor can borrow straight away, under Check Out Tool's usual rules.
  • INV-REG-6: A neighbor whose account is closed may sign up again, and doing so creates a new account.
    • The new account has its own neighbor ID. The closed account stays closed; it is never reopened.
  • INV-REG-7: Registering with a neighbor ID that is already used adds nothing new.
    • A repeat with the same name and email, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the account since. A repeat with different details is refused (neighbor-id-in-use).
  • INV-REG-8: Each account gets its own neighbor ID when it registers, and keeps it for good.
    • The neighbor ID is how every later event, view and command refers to the account. Names and emails are for people to read and for the shed to send email to.
  • INV-REG-9: Neighbor names need not be unique.
    • Two neighbors may both be called "Sam Lee". Accounts are told apart by neighbor ID, and only the email is checked for uniqueness.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-5, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: no account uses the email address ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up from the Sign Up screen as neighbor N1, with the name "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and the time it was recorded. Nothing waits for approval or email confirmation.
  • Whitespace is removed (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up with the name " Ana Ruiz " and the email " ana@example.org "
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org.
  • No name (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up with ana@example.org and a name that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with name-missing: "Please enter your name." No event is recorded.
  • No email (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up as "Ana Ruiz" with an email that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with email-missing: "Please enter your email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by an active account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N2 with ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by a suspended account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2 uses ben@example.org and is suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N3 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: Ana's account N1, using ana@example.org, was closed while active
    • When: Ana signs up as N4 with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N4, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N1 keeps its neighbor ID and stays closed.
  • Email of an account closed while suspended (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N5 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address is already used by an account." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended, reinstated, then closed (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was suspended, then reinstated, and then closed while active
    • When: Ben signs up as N9 with ben@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N9. The account wasn't suspended when it was closed, so its email is free again.
  • Different email after closing while suspended (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: Ben signs up as N5 with ben.new@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N5, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N2 stays closed.
  • Email an account has changed away from (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 registered with ana@oldmail.example and has since changed its email to ana@example.org
    • When: someone signs up as N6 with ana@oldmail.example
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N6. No account holds ana@oldmail.example any more.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-REG-9)
    • Given: Sam Lee's account N7 uses sam@example.org
    • When: another person signs up as N8, also named "Sam Lee", with sam.lee@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N8. There are two accounts named "Sam Lee".
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • The same request after the account was closed (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and N1 has since been closed
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. N1 stays closed.
  • A neighbor ID reused for different details (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: a Register Neighbor request arrives for N1 with "Ben Cole" and ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with neighbor-id-in-use: "That neighbor ID is already used by another account." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the person on the Sign Up screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

Reason Sentence Rule
name-missing Please enter your name. INV-REG-3
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-REG-3
email-in-use That email address is already used by an account. INV-REG-4
neighbor-id-in-use That neighbor ID is already used by another account. INV-REG-7

email-in-use is the same for every case in INV-REG-4, so a refused sign-up never reveals whether the other account is active, suspended, or closed while suspended.

neighbor-id-in-use can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same neighbor ID and the same name and email, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, even if the account has since been suspended, closed, or had its email changed. So a retry after a lost response never creates a second account. The repeat is recognised by its neighbor ID, and is checked before the email rule, so it is never refused as email-in-use by its own earlier registration.

Two sign-ups with the same email at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Registered happen as one step, so at most one is recorded. The other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. No email is sent on sign-up.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: anyone may sign up; signing up needs no existing account. How a neighbor is recognised afterwards, so that later actions are theirs, is the open identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Registered holds the neighbor's name and email address. It is read by the shed manager's screens (Neighbors, Tool Inventory, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors, Suspended Neighbors), by the neighbor's own My Account, and by the two email to-do lists. Whether any neighbor-facing screen shows another neighbor's name is the open question in Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) about showing who has a tool. Whether a closed account's details are kept for good is an open question below.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply INV-REG-4 and INV-REG-7, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (this slice): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Those slices aren't yet written in depth. These names are this slice's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors and My Account (a new entry); Tool Inventory, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the neighbor's name and email). Every later neighbor action (check out, hold, extend, return, change email, close account) and every shed-manager action on a neighbor refers to the account by its neighbor ID.

Open Questions

  • How does anyone identify themselves to the system, the shed manager and neighbors alike?
    • Signing up creates an account, but nothing in the model says how that person is recognised afterwards, so that a checkout or hold is theirs. The same question is open for the shed manager in Add Tool.
    • Options: (a) callers say who they are, and nothing checks it; (b) a sign-in outside the model supplies the neighbor's ID or the shed-manager role, with no new events; (c) sign-in and roles are modeled as events and slices.
    • Recommendation: (b). Neighbors need to be recognised before a loan can be theirs, and (b) adds nothing to the model.
  • What makes an email address acceptable at sign-up?
    • Options: (a) only that it is present; (b) a basic shape check (one "@", with text on both sides and a dot in the part after it), refused as email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address."
    • Recommendation: (b). A mistyped address otherwise only shows up later as an undelivered notice.
  • Are two emails that differ only in capital letters the same address?
    • For example, Ana@Example.org and ana@example.org.
    • Recommendation: yes for the one-account-per-email rule: compare without regard to case, and keep the address as typed. Otherwise one person can hold two accounts with the same mailbox.
  • Are there length limits on a neighbor's name and email?
    • Recommendation: name up to 100 characters, email up to 254. A longer one is refused with the limit in the reason, never cut short. This matches the limits proposed for tool names.
  • Does the shed's existing baseline of keeping personal data with the loan and hold history, with no erasure, carry over to neighbors' names and emails?
    • A closed account's email is needed to refuse a sign-up with the email of an account closed while suspended (INV-REG-4), and the closed account stays on the shed manager's Neighbors screen.
    • Recommendation: yes, it carries over: details are kept and never erased. If a neighbor must be able to have their details erased, that is a new event and slice.
  • What does a person see when they sign up with an email that can't be used?
    • INV-REG-4 refuses three cases with one reason, email-in-use, and the sentence "That email address is already used by an account." For an email held by an account closed while suspended, that sentence isn't true: the account is closed.
    • Options: (a) one reason and one sentence for all three cases, reworded to be true in each: "That email address can't be used to sign up."; (b) a separate reason for the closed-while-suspended case, telling the person why.
    • Recommendation: (a). It keeps one reason, never reveals another account's status, and stops the sentence misleading.
"},{"index":2,"name":"Check Out Tool","x0":438.75,"x1":582.75,"docHtml":"

Slice: Check Out Tool

Intent

Let a neighbor borrow a tool, self-service, from the Tool Catalog. The checkout opens a loan with a due date set from the tool's default checkout period, or from a shorter period the neighbor chooses. It is also how a holder collects a tool set aside for them: there is no separate pickup.

Trigger & Actor

The neighbor who will borrow the tool, from the Tool Catalog screen, on a tool the catalog offers Check Out on (available, reserved or set aside). The shed manager does not record checkouts. How the system recognises the neighbor is the open identity question in Add Tool (slices/add-tool.md); this slice follows its answer.

Command / Input

Command: Check Out Tool

A LoanId, ToolId or NeighborId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's checkedOutAt is that same moment.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new loan, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different loan already recorded (INV-CHK-12).
toolId ToolId yes The tool to borrow. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-CHK-11).
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor borrowing it, who must be the one making the request (INV-CHK-1). Must be a registered account (INV-CHK-11).
loanPeriodDays Int no Optional. Whole days, from 1 up to the tool's default checkout period (INV-CHK-6). When absent, the default applies. A fractional value is refused, never rounded.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Catalog @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Checked Out → context Loans Read by: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog and My Loans; My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire and Pickup Notices To Send (a holder's checkout ends their hold); Overdue Loans To Notify and Neighbors To Flag (the loan's due date); Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (loan details shown there).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command. Identifies the loan everywhere from here on.
toolId ToolId yes From the command.
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command: the borrower.
loanPeriodDays Int yes The period the loan started with: loanPeriodDays from the command, or the tool's default checkout period when it was absent.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the checkout date (today) plus loanPeriodDays. A later Loan Extended sets a new dueDate; this one never changes.
checkedOutAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment of the clock reading above. Its date in the shed's local time zone is the checkout date.

The event doesn't name the hold it ends. A holder has at most one hold on a tool, so readers match the ended hold by toolId and neighborId (INV-CHK-9).

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Checked Out changes the tool's entry in Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog, starts the loan's entry in My Loans, and ends the borrower's hold on the tool in My Holds and the hold to-do lists. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CHK-1: A neighbor checks a tool out themselves, for themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId, and the request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch otherwise). The shed manager does not record checkouts. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question.
  • INV-CHK-2: A tool that is already checked out can't be checked out again until it is returned or recorded lost.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan.
  • INV-CHK-3: A tool set aside for a holder can be checked out only by that holder, until the end of the collect-by date.
    • A tool is set aside from Hold Fulfilled for a hold until that hold ends. The collect-by date is Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate, recorded on the event; this slice reads it and never works it out.
    • The holder's pickup is an ordinary checkout. There is no separate pickup event.
  • INV-CHK-3a: A tool that is back in the shed with holds waiting, and not set aside, can be checked out only by the neighbor whose hold is at the front of the queue.
    • This holds after a return before Hold Fulfilled is recorded, and after a set-aside ends before the next hold is fulfilled.
    • The front of the queue is the hold on the tool, still waiting, whose Hold Placed was recorded first. Queue order is the order the Hold Placed events were recorded, never a comparison of times.
  • INV-CHK-3b: A holder's claim on a set-aside tool ends at the start of the day after the collect-by date, shed local time, whether or not Hold Expired has been recorded yet.
    • From that moment the set-aside is treated as ended. If a hold is waiting, only the neighbor at the front of the queue can check the tool out (INV-CHK-3a), and the former holder is refused. If none is waiting, anyone can, the former holder included.
  • INV-CHK-4: A retired tool can't be checked out.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it can't be checked out either.
  • INV-CHK-5: A neighbor with an overdue loan can't check out a tool.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while it is still open. The due date is the latest one set by Tool Checked Out or Loan Extended. Nothing records it; it is worked out from the due date and today.
    • Any open loan counts, including one whose tool has since been retired. A loan that ended because the tool was recorded lost no longer counts.
    • This also stops a holder collecting a tool set aside for them.
  • INV-CHK-6: The due date is set at checkout: the checkout date plus the loan period.
    • The loan period is the tool's default checkout period, unless the neighbor chooses a shorter one. It is never longer than the default.
    • A shorter period is chosen as a whole number of days, at least 1.
  • INV-CHK-7: A suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, and neither can a neighbor whose account is closed.
    • An account is suspended from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated, and closed for good from Neighbor Account Closed.
    • This also stops a suspended holder collecting a tool set aside for them. Their hold keeps its place, and the set-aside still lapses at the end of its collect-by date.
  • INV-CHK-8: There is no limit on how many tools one neighbor can have checked out at once.
  • INV-CHK-9: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The tool is then on loan, so it is not set aside for anyone, and the next hold waits for its return. When the tool comes back, the former holder is no longer in the queue.
    • The views that show holds end it by matching the checkout's toolId and neighborId; a holder has at most one hold on a tool.
  • INV-CHK-11: The tool must have been added, and the borrower must be a registered account.
  • INV-CHK-12: Checking out with a loan ID that is already used opens no new loan.
    • A repeat with the same tool, borrower and loan period succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the loan since. A repeat with different details is refused.
    • The loan period compared is the one the loan started with: a request that leaves the period out is the same as one that sends the tool's default explicitly.

Check Out is offered on a reserved or set-aside tool to every neighbor, not only to the holder whose turn it is (Tool Catalog, INV-TCAT-11). This slice refuses anyone else with the reason (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: the cordless drill (tool D) has a 7-day default checkout period, Ana, Ben and Cara are registered, active neighbors with no overdue loans, and today is 5 October.

  • Happy path (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill from the Tool Catalog as loan L1, keeping the default period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for L1: the drill, Ana, a 7-day period, due 12 October, checked out today.
  • Shorter period chosen (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 3-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 3-day period, due 8 October.
  • Shortest period (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 1-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 1-day period, due 6 October.
  • Period equal to the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 7-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 7-day period, due 12 October.
  • Period longer than the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with an 8-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Period of zero, or not whole (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with a 0-day period, or a 2.5-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Tool already checked out (INV-CHK-2)
    • Given: Ben has the drill on loan
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-checked-out: "This tool is already checked out." No event is recorded.
  • Retired tool (INV-CHK-4)
    • Given: the drill has been retired
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no tool T9 has been added
    • When: Ana tries to check out T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no account N9 has been registered
    • When: a request to check out the drill for N9 arrives
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't borrow tools while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana's account is closed
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana arrives
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Reinstated neighbor can borrow again (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has been reinstated, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Overdue loan blocks a checkout (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 4 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan: "You have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool." No event is recorded.
  • A loan due today is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 5 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • An extended loan is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 4 October, and Loan Extended moved it to 11 October
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • A loan ended by loss no longer blocks (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 1 October, and Tool Lost has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Several loans at once (INV-CHK-8)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder and the hedge trimmer on loan, neither overdue, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded. Ana now has three tools on loan.
  • Holder collects a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: Hold Fulfilled was recorded for Ben's hold on the drill with a collect-by date of 6 October, so the drill is set aside for him
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben, due 12 October. Ben's hold ends with it.
  • Holder collects on the collect-by date (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 5 October
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben.
  • Someone else tries to take a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 6 October
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with set-aside-for-another: "This tool is set aside for another neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Overdue holder can't collect (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben has the ladder on loan, due 2 October
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan. The drill stays set aside for Ben until his collect-by date ends.
  • Suspended holder can't collect (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended. His hold keeps its place.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, Ben's hold is at the front of its queue and Cara's is behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ben checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. Ben's hold ends without ever being fulfilled.
  • An early collector is out of the queue when the tool returns (INV-CHK-9, INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill as the front holder before his hold was fulfilled, with Cara's hold behind his. He has since returned it, and Cara's hold is still waiting.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill again
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded. Cara is now at the front.
  • Someone who isn't next tries to take a reserved tool (INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, with Ben's hold at the front and Cara's behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Cara tries to check out the drill, and then Ana does
    • Then: both are refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded.
  • Holder too late, another hold waiting (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben on 14 October, to collect by 17 October, and Cara's hold is waiting. Hold Expired has not yet been recorded.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: refused with pickup-window-ended: "Your pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue." No event is recorded. Cara can check the drill out.
  • Someone else tries a lapsed set-aside while a hold waits (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Ana, who has no hold on the drill, tries to check it out
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another. No event is recorded.
  • Next holder takes a lapsed set-aside before the expiry is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Cara checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Cara, and her hold ends. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by someone else (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben, to collect by 17 October, no other hold is waiting, and Hold Expired has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by the former holder (INV-CHK-3b, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: as above
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. His own checkout ends his hold, so no Hold Expired follows for it.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana, default period
    • When: the same Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. Ana still has one loan of the drill.
  • A loan ID reused for different details (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana
    • When: a Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives naming the ladder
    • Then: refused with loan-id-in-use: "That loan ID is already used by another loan." No event is recorded.
  • Someone checks out a tool for another neighbor (INV-CHK-1)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only check out tools for yourself." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the Tool Catalog screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. requester-mismatch (INV-CHK-1).
  2. The loan ID is already used (INV-CHK-12): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise loan-id-in-use.
  3. tool-not-found, then neighbor-not-found (INV-CHK-11).
  4. tool-retired (INV-CHK-4).
  5. tool-checked-out (INV-CHK-2).
  6. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-CHK-7).
  7. has-overdue-loan (INV-CHK-5).
  8. The tool's holds (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b):
    • set-aside-for-another: the tool is set aside and its collect-by date hasn't ended, and the requester isn't the holder.
    • pickup-window-ended: the set-aside's collect-by date has ended, another hold is waiting, and the requester is the former holder.
    • reserved-for-another: the tool is back with a hold waiting (or a lapsed set-aside with one waiting), and the requester isn't the neighbor at the front of the queue. This includes a third neighbor after a set-aside lapses.
  9. period-out-of-range (INV-CHK-6).
Reason Sentence Rule
loan-id-in-use That loan ID is already used by another loan. INV-CHK-12
requester-mismatch You can only check out tools for yourself. INV-CHK-1
tool-not-found There is no such tool. INV-CHK-11
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CHK-11
tool-retired This tool has been retired. INV-CHK-4
tool-checked-out This tool is already checked out. INV-CHK-2
account-closed This account is closed. INV-CHK-7
neighbor-suspended You can't borrow tools while your account is suspended. INV-CHK-7
has-overdue-loan You have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool. INV-CHK-5
set-aside-for-another This tool is set aside for another neighbor. INV-CHK-3
pickup-window-ended Your pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue. INV-CHK-3b
reserved-for-another This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue. INV-CHK-3a
period-out-of-range The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period. INV-CHK-6

loan-id-in-use, tool-not-found and neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same loan ID and the same tool, borrower and requested period succeeds and records nothing new, even if the loan has since been extended, returned or lost. So a retry after a lost response never opens a second loan.

Two neighbors checking out the same tool at the same moment: only one Tool Checked Out is recorded for the tool. The other request is refused with tool-checked-out, because each checkout is decided against the tool's loans as already recorded, one at a time.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may check out a tool only for themselves (INV-CHK-1); the shed manager doesn't check tools out. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question in Add Tool.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Checked Out links a neighbor to a tool and a due date. It holds no name or email; those stay on Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Checked Out (this slice): loanId, toolId, neighborId, loanPeriodDays, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId. Queue order is the order these events were recorded.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, tool-inventory.md, tool-catalog.md and register-neighbor.md. Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate is the Date the fulfiller records (set by the system, as dueDate is on loans). Those slices aren't yet written in depth, and each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire, Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors. Extend Loan, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost act on the loan by its loan ID.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":3,"name":"Extend Loan","x0":607.75,"x1":751.75,"docHtml":"

Slice: Extend Loan

Intent

Let a borrower keep a tool longer by extending their loan from My Loans. An extension moves the due date later by one of the tool's default checkout periods. It is refused while someone is waiting for the tool, once the loan is overdue, while the borrower is suspended, and once the tool has been retired.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from the My Loans screen, on one of their own loans that My Loans offers Extend on. How the system recognises the borrower is the open identity question in Add Tool (slices/add-tool.md); this slice follows its answer.

Command / Input

Command: Extend Loan

A LoanId is a UUID. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone. "Today" is that date at the moment the command is handled.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor extending, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-EXT-1).
loanId LoanId yes The loan to extend. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-EXT-9).
fromDueDate Date yes The due date the borrower is extending from, as My Loans showed it. Must be the loan's current due date, unless this exact extension has already been recorded (INV-EXT-10).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Loan Extended → context Loans Read by: My Loans, Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the new due date shown); Overdue Loans To Notify and Neighbors To Flag (when the loan becomes overdue, and whether a return is late); Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (loan details shown there).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
fromDueDate Date yes From the command: the loan's due date before this extension.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the new due date, fromDueDate plus the tool's default checkout period (INV-EXT-3).
extendedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

A later extension records a new Loan Extended; this one never changes. A loan's current due date is the dueDate of its latest Loan Extended, or of its Tool Checked Out if it has never been extended.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Loan Extended moves the loan's due date in My Loans, Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog, and in the lists that work out overdue loans and late returns. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-EXT-1: Only the borrower can extend a loan, and they do it themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId. The request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch), and the loan must be theirs: the neighbor who checked the tool out (not-your-loan). How the requester is recognised is the open identity question.
  • INV-EXT-2: Only an open loan can be extended.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan.
  • INV-EXT-3: An extension adds one of the tool's default checkout periods to the loan's current due date.
    • It adds the tool's default period even if the borrower chose a shorter period at checkout.
    • The default period is the one on Tool Added. It never changes.
  • INV-EXT-4: An extension is refused while any hold is waiting on the tool.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account. This is the meaning the Tool Catalog and Place Hold use.
    • My Loans shows the same (INV-MYL-9), except for a moment it can't see: when a lapsed set-aside has gone to the next holder and its Hold Expired isn't recorded yet. My Loans then holds back Extend for a few seconds; this slice already allows it.
    • Holds that were already waiting when the loan began count too.
  • INV-EXT-5: An extension is refused once the loan is overdue.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its current due date, in the shed's local time. On the due date itself, the loan can still be extended.
    • Only the overdue loan itself is refused. The same borrower can still extend their other loans that are not overdue.
  • INV-EXT-6: There is no limit on how many times a loan can be extended, as long as each extension meets the other rules here.
  • INV-EXT-7: A suspended neighbor can't extend a loan.
    • A neighbor is suspended from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated. Once reinstated, they can extend again.
    • A closed account has no open loans, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan, so it needs no rule here.
  • INV-EXT-8: A loan whose tool has been retired can't be extended.
    • The loan carries on until the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-EXT-9: The loan must exist.
  • INV-EXT-10: Extending from a due date that has already been extended from adds nothing.
    • A repeated request succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the loan since. A request whose fromDueDate is neither the loan's current due date nor one it has already been extended from is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana has the cordless drill on loan L1. The drill has a 7-day default checkout period. L1 is due 12 October, has never been extended, and no hold is waiting on the drill. Ana is active, and today is 10 October.

  • Happy path (INV-EXT-3)
    • Given: L1 as above
    • When: Ana extends L1 from My Loans, from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October.
  • Extending on the due date (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: today is 12 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Extending the day after the due date (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: today is 13 October, and L1 is still due 12 October
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1 from 12 October
    • Then: refused with loan-overdue: "This loan is overdue and can't be extended. Please return the tool." No event is recorded.
  • Extending again (INV-EXT-6)
    • Given: L1 has already been extended once and is due 19 October; today is 18 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 19 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, from 19 October to 26 October.
  • Extending a loan checked out for a shorter period (INV-EXT-3)
    • Given: Ana checked out the drill for 3 days, so L1 is due 8 October; today is 7 October
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 8 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 15 October: the drill's 7-day default, not 3 days.
  • A hold is waiting (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ben has placed a hold on the drill, and it is still waiting
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with hold-waiting: "Someone is waiting for this tool, so this loan can't be extended." No event is recorded.
  • A hold was waiting when the loan began (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ana checked out the drill as the front holder, and Cara's hold was behind hers and is still waiting
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with hold-waiting.
  • The waiting hold has ended (INV-EXT-4)
    • Given: Ben placed a hold on the drill, and then cancelled it
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Another of the borrower's loans is overdue (INV-EXT-5)
    • Given: Ana also has the ladder on loan, due 4 October, so it is overdue
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded for L1, to 19 October. The ladder loan is still overdue.
  • Suspended borrower (INV-EXT-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't extend loans while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Reinstated borrower (INV-EXT-7)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has been reinstated
    • When: Ana extends L1 from 12 October
    • Then: Loan Extended is recorded, to 19 October.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-EXT-8)
    • Given: the drill was retired while Ana has it on loan
    • When: Ana tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired, so this loan can't be extended. Please return it by the due date." No event is recorded.
  • Loan already returned (INV-EXT-2)
    • Given: Ana has returned the drill, ending L1
    • When: a request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Loan ended by loss (INV-EXT-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost has been recorded for L1
    • When: a request to extend L1 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended.
  • Unknown loan (INV-EXT-9)
    • Given: no loan L9 has been checked out
    • When: a request to extend L9 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-EXT-1)
    • Given: L1 is Ana's loan
    • When: Ben, naming himself, tries to extend L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only extend your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request that doesn't come from the neighbor it names (INV-EXT-1)
    • Given: L1 is Ana's loan
    • When: a request to extend L1, naming Ana, comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only extend loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: Loan Extended was recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October
    • When: the same request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. L1 is still due 19 October.
  • The same request after a hold was placed (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: Loan Extended was recorded for L1, from 12 October to 19 October, and Ben has since placed a hold on the drill
    • When: the same request to extend L1 from 12 October arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Extending from a due date that isn't current (INV-EXT-10)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October and has never been extended
    • When: a request to extend L1 from 5 October arrives
    • Then: refused with due-date-changed: "This loan's due date has changed. Check it and try again." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. requester-mismatch (INV-EXT-1).
  2. loan-not-found (INV-EXT-9).
  3. not-your-loan (INV-EXT-1).
  4. If a Loan Extended for this loan already has the same fromDueDate, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-EXT-10).
  5. loan-ended (INV-EXT-2).
  6. due-date-changed, if fromDueDate isn't the loan's current due date (INV-EXT-10).
  7. neighbor-suspended (INV-EXT-7).
  8. tool-retired (INV-EXT-8).
  9. loan-overdue (INV-EXT-5).
  10. hold-waiting (INV-EXT-4).
Reason Sentence Rule
requester-mismatch You can only extend loans for yourself. INV-EXT-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-EXT-9
not-your-loan You can only extend your own loans. INV-EXT-1
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-EXT-2
due-date-changed This loan's due date has changed. Check it and try again. INV-EXT-10
neighbor-suspended You can't extend loans while your account is suspended. INV-EXT-7
tool-retired This tool has been retired, so this loan can't be extended. Please return it by the due date. INV-EXT-8
loan-overdue This loan is overdue and can't be extended. Please return the tool. INV-EXT-5
hold-waiting Someone is waiting for this tool, so this loan can't be extended. INV-EXT-4

loan-not-found and requester-mismatch can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed loan ID (not a UUID), or a fromDueDate that isn't a date, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: each extension is identified by the loan and the due date it extends from. A double submit, or a retry after a lost response, carries the same fromDueDate, so it succeeds with nothing recorded, even if the loan has since changed. It never extends the loan twice.

Two requests for the same loan at the same moment: each is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time, so only one Loan Extended is recorded from a given due date.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the borrower may extend their own loan (INV-EXT-1). The shed manager doesn't extend loans. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question in Add Tool.
  • PII & compliance: Loan Extended holds only the loan and its dates. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, checkedOutAt.
    • Loan Extended (this slice): loanId, fromDueDate, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold), Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, check-out-tool.md, tool-inventory.md and tool-catalog.md. This slice adds fromDueDate and extendedAt to Loan Extended; readers that only need the new due date keep reading {loanId, dueDate}.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Overdue Loans To Notify, Neighbors To Flag, Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (the new due date).

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":4,"name":"Overdue Loans To Notify","x0":776.75,"x1":920.75,"docHtml":"

Slice: Overdue Loans To Notify

Intent

The list of overdue loans whose borrowers have not yet been sent an overdue notice. The overdue notice gateway works through it, so each borrower with an overdue loan is emailed once, as soon as the loan is overdue. Each item carries everything the email needs, so the gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Overdue Notice Gateway, a system reaction in the Send Overdue Notice slice. No person reads this list, and it has no screen.
  • What the gateway does with it: for each loan on the list, it hands one notice to the email provider and records Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice slice). How often it checks the list is that slice's concern.

Read Model / View

  • View: Overdue Loans To Notify built from events: "Tool Added", "Neighbor Registered", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Overdue Notice Sent", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Overdue Notice Gateway (Send Overdue Notice). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a loan is overdue is worked out when the list is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so a loan is on the list from the first read after midnight following its due date.

The view keeps one row for every open loan that hasn't been sent a notice; the query returns only the overdue ones. LoanId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId Tool Checked Out.loanId.
toolId ToolId Tool Checked Out.toolId.
neighborId NeighborId Tool Checked Out.neighborId: the borrower.
dueDate Date Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for this loan.
toolName Text Derived: Tool Added.name for toolId, copied under this name.
borrowerName Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.name for neighborId, copied under this name.
borrowerEmail Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.email for neighborId, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for that neighbor, copied under this name. Always the current one.
overdue Bool Derived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate (INV-OLN-1). Worked out when the list is read.

Bookkeeping. To fill toolName, borrowerName and borrowerEmail the moment a loan starts, the view keeps the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and the name of every tool, not only those on a row. This is never returned except on the rows the query returns.

When a row leaves the view. A loan's row is removed when Overdue Notice Sent, Tool Returned or Tool Lost is recorded for it (INV-OLN-8). Nothing puts it back.

Queries

  • List loans to notify. Takes nothing. Returns every row whose overdue is yes, with loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, toolName, borrowerName and borrowerEmail. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the gateway, which sends one notice per loan.

Invariants / Business Rules

A loan is ready for its notice as soon as it joins the list. When the email goes out, with no quiet hours, is Send Overdue Notice's rule (INV-OVN-6, Send Overdue Notice).

  • INV-OLN-1: A loan is on the list from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while the tool is still out and no overdue notice has been sent for it.
    • Overdue is worked out by comparing the due date with today. No event marks a loan overdue; the loan joins the list because the date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-2: A loan's due date is the one set at checkout, moved by each extension.
    • A loan extended before it became overdue joins the list only once its new due date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-3: Once an overdue notice is sent for a loan, the loan leaves the list and never comes back.
    • One notice per loan. An overdue loan can't be extended (INV-EXT-5, Extend Loan), so it stays overdue until it ends, and no second notice goes out.
  • INV-OLN-4: When the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost, its loan leaves the list.
    • A loan that ends this way before its notice went out never gets a notice.
    • A closed account never has a loan on the list, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
    • A loan whose tool is retired while it is out stays on the list and still gets its notice: the loan carries on until the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-OLN-6: Each loan on the list carries everything the notice needs: the borrower's name and email, the tool's name, and the due date.
    • The borrower's name comes from Neighbor Registered, and the email is the borrower's current one: Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The tool's name comes from Tool Added, and the due date from Tool Checked Out, moved by any Loan Extended. The gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.
  • INV-OLN-8: A loan leaves the list only when an overdue notice is sent for it, when the tool is returned, or when the tool is recorded lost.
    • A notice that later fails to deliver doesn't put the loan back on the list. The failure is shown to the shed manager on Undelivered Notices, and no further attempt is made.
  • INV-OLN-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Loan not yet overdue (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: Ana (N1) borrowing the cordless drill (T1), due 12 October
    • When: the list is read at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is not returned.
  • Loan becomes overdue (INV-OLN-1, INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org; Tool Added for T1, "Cordless drill"; and L1 is due 12 October, still out
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is returned, with toolName "Cordless drill", borrowerName "Ana Ruiz", borrowerEmail ana@example.org, and dueDate 12 October.
  • Extended before it became overdue (INV-OLN-2)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for L1 on 10 October, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: L1 is not returned when the list is read on 13 October, and is returned from 00:00 on 20 October if still out.
  • Overdue notice sent (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-8)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and is never returned again while the drill is out.
  • Returned before the notice (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1 before any notice is sent
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October and still out, and Tool Retired was recorded for T1 on 11 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned, ready for its notice.
  • Borrower changes their email (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is on the list, carrying ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana@example.org
    • Then: L1 stays on the list, now carrying ana@example.org, so the notice goes to the new address.
  • Email changed before the loan is overdue (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October, and N1's email was changed to ana@example.org on 10 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned carrying ana@example.org.
  • Several borrowers (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: L1 (Ana, due 12 October) and L2 (Ben, due 14 October) are both out
    • When: the list is read on 13 October
    • Then: only L1 is returned.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: L1 is on the list once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out for L1 is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still on the list once.
  • Replayed sent notice (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, so L1 is off the list
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Sent is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still off the list.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-OLN-9). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a loan that has left the list: once a loan's row is removed, a later Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost for it (a replay) changes nothing. An Overdue Notice Failed doesn't reach this list at all.
  • The gateway reads a loan twice before Overdue Notice Sent lands: the list may return the same loan on two reads in a row. Sending one notice per loan is the Send Overdue Notice slice's rule, enforced when it records Overdue Notice Sent; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Overdue Notice Gateway. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and hands them to the gateway only for borrowers with an overdue loan. It shows them on no screen.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. A loan is ready as soon as it joins the list; how soon the email goes out after that is Send Overdue Notice's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/extend-loan.md and slices/my-loans.md. Change Email, Send Overdue Notice, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Send Overdue Notice, whose gateway works from this list and records Overdue Notice Sent.

Open Questions

None.
